new_flaw.description: The search loop that replaces _advanceToNextDown in reset does not stop at the end tick. It keeps loading lower bitmap words until it finds any initialized tick, and stops only at word type(int16).min. Gas therefore grows with the distance to the next initialized tick below the start, not with the swap range.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 10, only position [100, 200), pool tick 50 with no active liquidity. A taxed zero-for-one swap moves the tick from 50 to 40. Each of the two reset calls loads every word from 0 down to -32768, about 32,800 external reads, so the swap runs out of gas. The post-hoc gas check in this folder (forge_P7_posthoc.json) used about 150 million gas for such a swap. With tick spacing 1 and only a full-range position, a one-tick swap near tick 0 makes each reset load about 3,500 words.

claude-opus-5-5.reason: The loop has no end-tick check and runs to word type(int16).min when no initialized tick lies below, which the post-hoc gas check confirms at about 150 million gas.

gpt-6.1-sol.reason: It reported no flaw, but it missed the unbounded word scan in reset.

summary: The repair replaces the call to _advanceToNextDown with its own loop that finds the highest initialized tick at or below compress(startTick). If that tick is above the end tick it becomes currentTick, otherwise hasNext is false. The ticks returned are correct in every case, but the loop does not stop at the end tick.
